point-in-time correctness.simple: Each training row uses only feature values that were known at that row's time, never later values.
point-in-time correctness.example: A label on Tuesday 15:00 uses the feature computed Tuesday 02:00, not Wednesday's.

feature store.simple: A system that stores feature values with their timestamps and serves them for both training and live predictions.
feature store.example: Feast is an open-source feature store.

offline store.simple: The part of a feature store that keeps the full history of features. It builds training sets.
offline store.example: A data warehouse table of daily features.

online store.simple: The part of a feature store that keeps only the latest value per entity so a model can read it in milliseconds.
online store.example: A key-value database with the latest orders_7d per store.

training-serving skew.simple: A difference between the data the model saw in training and the data it sees when serving.
training-serving skew.example: A feature computed in SQL for training and in Java for serving drifts apart.

merge_asof.simple: A pandas join that matches each row to the nearest earlier (or later) row of another table by time.

data leakage.simple: Using information in training that will not exist at prediction time. Scores look good but fail in real use.
data leakage.example: Using next week's average to predict next Monday.

tolerance.simple: In merge_asof, the largest time gap allowed between a row and its match.
tolerance.example: tolerance=pd.Timedelta('1D') rejects features older than one day.

pipeline.simple: A chain of automatic steps: get data, build features, predict, save results.

batch prediction.simple: Running the model on a schedule to produce many forecasts at once.
batch prediction.example: Every night at 02:00, forecast 14 days for 5,000 stores.

online prediction.simple: Running the model when a request arrives and returning one answer in milliseconds.
online prediction.example: An ETA shown to a customer right after an order.

champion-challenger.simple: Test a new model (challenger) next to the live model (champion) and promote it only if it wins.
champion-challenger.example: Run the new model for two weeks on the same data.

shadow mode.simple: A new model makes predictions in production but nobody uses them. You only compare.
shadow mode.example: Log the new forecast next to the live one.

backfill.simple: Re-running a pipeline for past dates, for example after a bug fix.
backfill.example: Recompute forecasts for last month with the fixed feature.

idempotent.simple: Running a job twice gives the same result as running it once.
idempotent.example: An upsert by key is idempotent. An append is not.

data drift.simple: The input data (features) look different from the training data. Also called covariate shift.
data drift.example: A new customer group has bigger baskets.

concept drift.simple: The relation between inputs and the target changes, even if the inputs look the same.
concept drift.example: After a price rise, the same traffic gives fewer sales.

Population Stability Index.simple: A number that compares two distributions bin by bin. Higher means a bigger shift. Often written PSI.
Population Stability Index.example: PSI below 0.1 is stable; above 0.25 is a large shift.

MAD.simple: Mean absolute deviation: the average of the absolute forecast errors. Same as MAE.

WAPE.simple: Weighted absolute percentage error: sum of absolute errors divided by sum of actual values.
WAPE.example: Absolute errors total 25 on actuals totaling 300: WAPE = 8.3%.

tracking signal.simple: The running sum of forecast errors divided by the running MAD. It grows when a forecast is biased in one direction.
tracking signal.example: A tracking signal above 4 is a common alarm.

local model.simple: A model fitted separately for each time series.

global model.simple: One model trained on many series together.
global model.example: A LightGBM model with lag features for all products.

cold start.simple: A new item has little or no history, so a model cannot learn from it directly.
